title: Prompt header fingerprinting with multi-model aliasing and slab-aware eviction
creator: Ayesha Khatri
description: Problem: Our current KV prefix reuse identifies cacheable prompt segments by exact bytes and full hashes. This misses near-duplicates (templated prompts, model aliases) and fragments cache space with many low-value entries. Goal: implement a prompt-header fingerprinting pipeline that canonicalizes template slots, groups semantically-equivalent prefixes across model variants, and packs KV slices into GPU slabs for better memory density. The feature should integrate with continuous batching so dedup decisions avoid increasing P99 latency and should support gradual rollout and metrics-driven rollback.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prefix fingerprinting reduces unique KV entries by >= 30% on benchmark traces without regression to P99 latency (>5% acceptable for first rollout). 2) Slab-aware allocator increases average occupancy of GPU KV slabs by >= 18%. 3) Dedup pipeline handles multi-model aliasing (model v1/v1-quant/v2-compatible) with correct routing to compatible kernel paths. 4) Feature toggle and canary path implemented; rollout controlled by token-level cost delta and P99 SLOs. 5) Benchmarks, dashboards, and a retrospective doc produced.
design_summary: We will compute a stable 'prompt header' that strips non-semantic tokens (timestamps, user IDs) via a configurable template extractor and then compute two signatures: (a) a compact canonical hash for exact-match lookup and fast routing, (b) a locality-preserving SimHash for approximate grouping. Group keys will be mapped through a multi-model alias table so identical logical prompts served by different model variants share cached KV segments where execution paths are compatible. A slab-aware allocator will pack KV fragments into 4KB-aligned GPU slabs with a small freelist to reduce fragmentation. Eviction will combine LRU recency with reuse frequency and slab compactability heuristics.
implementation_notes: - Add template extraction rules in runtime config with safe defaults (common patterns). - Add two-stage signature compute in hot path: fast byte-level canonicalization + 64b canonical hash; async simhash computation for background consolidation. - Maintain an alias graph {logical_signature -> [model_variants]} for routing and compatibility checks. - Extend KV store metadata with slab_id, offset, compactable_flag. - Slab allocator implemented in native layer (cuda memmgr) with hooks for reclaim and defragmentation during low-util windows. - Continuous batching: fingerprint lookup happens at batch ingress, de-dup merge reduces work items; ensure this is bounded (max merges per batch) to avoid tail effects. - Telemetry: per-key reuse_count, eviction_reason, slab_occupancy, merge_latency.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Extra computation at request ingress could increase P50/P99 latency. Mitigation: keep canonical hash compute inlined and offload simhash to background consolidation; add circuit-breaker to bypass fingerprinting under high tail latency. Risk: cross-model reuse may violate kernel compatibility, causing incorrect outputs. Mitigation: strict compatibility checks and fallback to model-specific cache paths; unit tests covering kernel mismatch cases. Risk: slab compaction pauses could interfere with inference. Mitigation: schedule compaction during low load and throttle compaction bandwidth.
testing_plan: - Unit tests: canonicalizer, hash collisions, alias mapping, slab allocator invariants. - Integration tests: end-to-end caching for templated prompts with multiple model variants. - Perf tests: replay 72h production trace on canary infra to measure unique KV entries, slab occupancy, P50/P95/P99 latency, token cost delta. - Chaos tests: simulate GPU OOM, high batch ingress, and ensure circuit-breaker and fallback work correctly. - Comparison runs against baseline (no fingerprinting).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated behind runtime flag; default off for all customers. 2) Canary group: internal traffic + 5% of small customers. 3) Monitor metrics for 48h: P99 latency, rejection rate, token-cost-per-1000-tokens, slab occupancy. 4) If metrics within thresholds, progressively increase to 25% then 100% over 4 weeks. 5) Rapid rollback path via console toggle and kill-switch in control plane.
